projects.name: 2.1.2.1; Establishment of Bio-buisnesses and GEBR livelihoods in two Biosphere Reserves and one protected site in Nigeria (Oban Biosphere Reserve, Omo Biosphere Reserve (BR) and Shere Hills Forest Reserve
projects.description:
The goal of the project is to reduce poverty and contribute to sustainable development and biodiversity in Omo Biosphere Reserve, Oban Biosphere Reserve in Nigeria, and Shere Hills Reserve through the establishment of green economy activities, with a focus on youth and women. Objectives are to -
1) Diversify and improve local economy through improved and alternative green biodiversity related livelihoods.
2) Build the capacity of communities in a holistic manner to ensure the sustainability of the biodiversity businesses,
3) Enable completion of nomination dossier for Shere Hills Reserve to join the World Network of Biosphere reserve

The project will be articulated along one outcomes and several outputs and activities, as described below.
 
Outcome 1: Reduce anthropogenic pressure on the forest, preserve biodiversity, diversify the local economy and improve biodiversity-related livelihoods.
 
This outcome will be achieved through the following outputs and activities.Output 1.1:   strengthened capacity of the Ministry of Environment, Forestry Research institute of Nigeria, National MAB committee, National Park Service and indeed other relevant stakeholders  to continue to provide support to community partners even after the end of the project funding.
 
Activity 1.1.1:   Inauguration of Project
Activity 1.1.2:   Capacity building on GEBR and conservation concepts 
 
Output 1.2:  Improved knowledge on socio-economic, biodiversity and market aspects available to stakeholders
 
Activity 1.2.1:  Stakeholder mapping, Community consultation and needs assessment;
Activity 1.2.2 : Socio-economic survey/Inquiry;
Activity 1.2.3:  Biodiversity  inventory (Biosphere Reserve/Protected area);
Activity 1.2.4:  Market Survey and Product analyses;
Activity 1.2.5: Validation workshop.
 
Output 1.3: Local communities have enhanced capacity to reduce their environmental impact, develop alternative livelihood activities, and manage their biodiversity businesses including accounting, product marketing, packaging, sales and use and maintenance of simple business equipment.
 
Activity 1.3.1: Training on environmental education - management and biodiversity conservation.
Activity 1.3.2:  Training on business management, processes and bookkeeping.
Activity 1.3.3:  Small business incubation support through hands-on training and coaching on business start-up processes.
Activity 1.3.4: Technical training on the use and maintenance of simple biodiversity business equipment.
 
Output 1.4 :  Alternative livelihoods established and economy diversified
 
Activity 1.4.1: Procurement of tools and appliances, or simple inputs for the establishment of selected biodiversity livelihood activities;
Activity 1.4.2:  Facilitation for the establishment of selected biodiversity livelihoods in target areas (at least 30% Female and 20% youth);
Activity 1.4.3: Comprehensive start-up business incubation services, coaching and mentoring of project participants on the management of their biodiversity livelihood activities.
Activity 1.4.4. Support business networks development, including towards access to micro-finance, cooperatives, development of sales channels, profit re-investment, and knowledge of vendors and providers for inputs.
 
Output 1.5 :  Designation of Shere Hills Reserve as a Biosphere Reserve in the World Network of Biosphere Reserve (WNBR)  
Activity 1.5.1: Production of zonation Maps  
Activity 1.5.2:  Consultations with the communities
Activity 1.5.3 Completion and processing of Biosphere reserve nomination dossier
Implementation strategy.
Activity 1.1.1-2 Inauguration and capacity building at National authorities’ level
 At inauguration, the project will be presented to the relevant stakeholders and partners; while also receiving inputs on strategies of implementation and their roles. Following the inauguration, the next activity will be a capacity building on the concept of GEBR; for the Ministry of Environment, Forestry Research institute of Nigeria, National MAB committee, National Park Service and indeed other relevant stakeholders to continue to provide support to community partners even after the end of the project funding. This will ensure sustainability of the project activities.
Activities 1.2.1-4:  Mapping and assessments
 The mapping and assessment is aimed at ensuring the full involvement of the target communities in the framework of the opportunities offered by the natural environment in the selected areas. This first activity is about identifying and bringing together community partners and all relevant stakeholders, to discuss and develop a shared vision for the whole project and the prospective biodiversity business. Stakeholder aspirations, roles, responsibilities and capacities in the project will be reviewed. The project will take stock of the indigenous knowledge of the communities, and this will be an invaluable tool for the choice of the biodiversity businesses.
 
The second activity will be a socio-economic survey and needs assessment. The main objective of the study is to provide baseline data on the socio-economic status of the local communities, which will serve as the benchmark for measuring the project impacts[1]. Information on livelihoods, gender perspectives and natural resource utilization in the target sites will be gathered.
 
The third activity will be the Biosphere Reserve Assessment and Inventory. An in-depth assessment and biological inventory exercise will be carried out for all the target intervention areas with the specific aim of obtaining the biodiversity index of the park.  The results of the inventory will guide the choice and design of biodiversity business initiatives in the different areas. It will also guide the delineation of the proposed biosphere reserve (core, buffer and transition zones), which will be instrumental for the Biosphere Reserve nomination dossiers.
 
The fourth and last activity is Market Survey and Product Analyses. This activity is aimed at ensuring that careful analyses of the opportunities and limitations involved with the biodiversity business are carried out.  This would include the review of markets, availability and sustainability of resources, environmental, infrastructural and policy and other barriers to the development of the business. Special attention will be given to the involvement of the private sector, of business intermediaries and on the logistic aspects of the market analysis.
 
Activity 1.2.5: Validation/launch workshops
After the start-up phase and studies, 2 validation workshops will be organized (one per site) to bring together all relevant stakeholders to validate the results of all socio-economic, market and biodiversity studies. Community leaders and potential community partners and project beneficiaries will be sensitized and confirm their engagement in the implementation of project activities. During the workshop, the selection of the livelihood business will be confirmed by all stakeholders.
  
Activities 1.3.1-4:  Capacity building at community level
As emerges from the livelihood analysis, capacity building is an important element in supporting new and improved livelihoods for local communities.  Communities in both sites will be trained in a variety of practical skills for the development and management of their selected biodiversity businesses. In addition to the skills necessary to undertake production, community partners will acquire skills in the fields of accounting, marketing, packaging of their products, managing their business and re-investing their business profit. Different training sessions will be organized on the following topics:
1.	Environmental and biodiversity conservation education;
2.	Accounting, marketing and packaging;
3.	Hands on training on implementation of alternative livelihood activities;
4.	Technical training on the use and maintenance of the equipment.
 To ensure that capacity is strengthened at different levels, additional training materials would be developed in a language and style that corresponds to the literacy level of stakeholders and community partners. Ultimately, communities will be trained to monitor and manage the natural resources on which their business depends. Conservation and environmental education will therefore be an integral part of this project. This will ensure that the link between biodiversity conservation and development is maintained. Community members will also learn to continuously re-invest part of their income to ensure the sustainability of their subsistence revenues.
 
Activities 1.4.1-4:  Implementation of green economy activities. 
A business implementation structure will be drawn up and the service or production will be rolled out. The community partners and beneficiaries will be provided with start-up support and inputs for their businesses in the form of tools and equipment. Relevant items will be purchased and distributed and community partners will receive training on how to use them. For example, those who will choose a livelihood such as beekeeping will receive improved hives, protective clothing and other tools for harvesting honey.
 
The plan will also include various approaches towards attracting other investors. Suitable assessed Green businesses mostly preferred by women and the youth will be targeted so that at least 30% of community partners are female and 30% are youth. Incentives and benefit sharing mechanisms will be developed and will be engrained in the business structure and model of the enterprises that will be run by community partners in the form of cooperatives, or of small family businesses. This will ensure that hard working individuals are not only remunerated but are also incentivized. Project beneficiaries will be encouraged to form Cooperative Associations based on their livelihoods to ensure accountability, ownership and sustainability of their businesses.
 
Activity 1.5.1-3
Biosphere reserves promote solutions reconciling the conservation of biodiversity with its sustainable use. They are learning areas for sustainable development under diverse ecological, social and economic contexts, touching the lives of people that leave within its vicinity. Biosphere Reserves allow through research, the recreation of landscapes that have been affected by human activity, identify species that have disappeared, monitor climate change processes, for seeking recovery of ecosystems and their components and make better decisions. Considering that framework of Biosphere Reserve can guide and reinforce and sustain projects that enhance livelihoods, it will be useful to designate the Shere Hills Reserve as a Biosphere reserve. SHR is already a protected area and as such the project team with work with the Nigeran National MAB committee to use exiting and approved Guidelines to process the designation of SHR as a Biosphere reserve. This process include producing zonation maps (Maps of the core, buffer and transition zones), holding at least 4 consultation meetings and thorough completion of the Biosphere reserve nomination forms

projects.description:
UNESCO Abuja is joining efforts with the National Water Resources Institute, Kaduna, Nigeria, to implement the project “Improving Groundwater Governance towards achieving Sustainable Water Security for Human Settlements in Nigeria” in the framework of UNESCO/K-FIT Project “Water Security for Human Settlements in Developing Countries under Climate Change”. 

The project has the overall objective of improving knowledge-based management and governance of groundwater resources to support Nigeria in achieving sustainable water security for human settlements as well as build resilience to the impact of climate change. 

Specific objectives include:

projects.description:
Beyond the effect of COVID-19, inclusion in education is further challenged in Nigeria due to emerging insecurities that have threatened the safety of schools and ultimately denying some learners their right to education. As a result of the crises of insecurity, children of school age in some parts of Nigeria, particularly the Northern region have limited and in some cases no access to school. More worrisome, is the plight of learners with special needs, as infrastructure/equipment to aid their learnings are not available. The increasing emergencies that interrupt school systems and ultimately learning requires systemic preparedness that will ensure that learning continues without leaving anyone behind.

 It is in this regards that the implementation of the right to education, including creating lifelong learning opportunities will be pursued within the 42 C5 programmes and activities. To achieve this, UNEESCO will strengthen partnerships and networks to promote cross-sectoral collaboration that will stimulate technical dialogues, policies and practices that assures the learning needs of marginalized groups.
ICH will be addressed through Education, and States including the FCT, would be engaged to review ESP to ensure inclusive education is mainstreamed and budgeted for. Cross-sectoral collaboration with health, nutrition and social protection will be encouraged.

With number of crises affected areas increasing, there is need to apply the inclusive approach to education system and ensure no one is left behind. UNESCO is committed to taking concerted action to eliminate all forms of exclusions and marginalization, to uphold the right to education for all, to address disparities and inequalities in access, and in quality of learning, as well as to build education systems that are resilient and responsive to contemporary challenges. It implies focusing on those at greatest risk of being left behind and addressing inequalities in the education policies and practices. In view of this, UNESCO Abuja would:

i.      Support multistakeholder dialogues on facilitating inclusive education in Nigeria.
ii.    Work with the Nigeria’s Governors forum to advocate for policies and practices that promotes inclusive education in all states of the federation.
iii.   Support technical dialogues for addressing the learning needs of marginalized groups through inclusive policies.
iv. Support states to review and or development an ESP that ensures that inclusion is mainstreamed and budgeted for.

children.name: Output 1.2.1: Relevant Policies and Strategies for Improved Access to Decent Jobs are Reviewed/Developed Especially for Women Young People, Old Persons, Persons with Disabilities and Other Vulnerable Groups.

Output 1.2.2 Strengthened Capacity of Public and Private Sectors, and Civil Society Organisations to Implement Responsive Employment Programmes and Initiatives Including on Digital Skills and Green Economy.
Output 1.2.3: Improved Access to Markets and Financial Services for Women, Youth, Older Persons, Persons with Disabilities and Other Vulnerable Groups.

Output 1.2.4: Strengthened Capacity of Public and Private Sector and Civil Society Organisations to Implement Policies, Programmes and Strategies to Accelerate Harnessing of the Demographic Dividend for Sustainable Development.
children.description: This output focuses on building the capacity of public and private sector institutions and civil society organizations to effectively implement policies, programmes, and strategies that support the harnessing of the demographic dividend. It emphasizes enhancing coordination, technical skills, and institutional systems to deliver integrated, youth-focused initiatives in areas such as education, health, skills development, and employment. Through training, technical assistance, and stakeholder engagement, the output aims to enable more inclusive and impactful interventions that contribute to sustainable development.

children.name: Outcome 1.3: Improved Social Protection Coverage
children.description: By 2027, all people living in Nigeria have improved social protection coverage that are inclusive, gender responsive, age friendly and shock responsive, including social assistance, social insurance, and labour market interventions.

children.name: Output 1.3.1: Social Protection System Strengthening Through Improved Policy and Legal Framework at Both National and Sub-national Levels.
children.description:
Advocating for the scale up and expansion of social protection programs and support strengthening of policies, strategies and legal frameworks at
Abia Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross River, Enugu, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Lagos, Niger, Ogun, Ondo, Oyo, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe, and Zamfara

children.name: Output 1.3.2: Expanding Social Protection Schemes to more People Living in Nigeria Especially Women, Youth, Persons Living with Disabilities, Older Persons, People in the Informal Sector and Other Vulnerable Groups.
Outcome 1.4: Improved Data
children.description: By 2027, Nigeria has improved data for evidence based and risk informed planning and decision making.

children.name: Output 1.4.1: Strengthen Data Systems for Evidence-based Planning and Budgeting for Inclusive Economic Growth and Development, Including Advocating for Its Use.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 2: Clean Energy, Food Systems, Environmental Protection & Climate Change Resilience
framework.description:
Planet Pillar: Environmental Protection & Climate Change Resilience
People living in Nigeria particularly the most vulnerable have equitable access to affordable clean energy, enjoy sustainable food systems, healthy and clean environmental conditions and increased resilience to climate change and disasters.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which are:
1) Improved food security and nutrition, environmental sustainability, and sustainable natural resources management.
2) Improved management of climate change risks and building resilience to climate induced shocks
 3) Inclusive policies and practices for resilience and disaster risk management (DRM)

children.name: Outcome 2.1: Improved Food Security & Nutrition
children.description:
By 2027, Nigeria benefits from improved food security and nutrition, and sustainable food systems and environment and natural resources management.

The prioritized transformative initiative that will be implemented under this outcome is the transforming Nigeria's food systems.

children.name: Output 2.1.1: Institutions and Small-holder Farmers and Processors Strengthened to Deliver Sustained Food Production Systems that are Innovative, Resilient and Climate-smart for Enhanced Access to Food and Prevent Malnutrition, Especially within Vulnerable Communities.
Output 2.1.2: Control of Desertification, Degradation and Ensuring Sustainable Forest Management.

Output 2.1.3: Normative Frameworks, Institutions, and Systems Strengthened for Conservation, Sustainable use and Equitable Benefit Sharing from use of Biodiversity and Natural Resources to Ensure Environmental Sustainability for Development.
Output 2.1.4: Improvement of the Capacity to Ensure Integrated Water Resource Management at all Levels Including Transboundary Cooperation or Restoration of Water Related Ecosystems.
Outcome 2.2: Improved management of Climate
children.description: By 2027, Nigeria is implementing improved management of climate change risk and building resilience to adapt to its long term impact through the NDCs, sustainable energy production/consumption and climate finance.

children.name: Output 2.2.1: Human and Institutional Capacities of Public and Private Institutions at Federal, State and LGA Levels Strengthened to Develop and Implement Risk Management and (National) Adaptation Plans to Mitigate for Impact of Climate Change.
Output 2.2.2: Institutions and Systems Strengthened, and Solutions Adopted to Reduce Pollution and Increase Access to Clean, Affordable and Sustainable Energy.
Output 2.2.3: Policy, Legal and Institutional Frameworks Developed/Strengthened for Sustainable Energy Development and Management.
Output 2.2.4: Human and Institutional Capacity Developed and Strengthened to Access Global and Other Innovative Climate Financing Mechanisms.
Outcome 2.3: Policies & practices for resilience & DRM
children.description: By 2027, Nigeria implements inclusive policies and practices for Resilience and Disaster Risk management for risk informed development.

children.name: Output 2.3.1: Improved IHR Capacities.
Output 2.3.2: Strengthen Response to Emerging Migration and Urbanisation Patterns Including Settlement in Crisis.
Output 2.3.3: Improved National and Local Disaster Risk Reduction Capacities and Index.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3: Inclusive & Equitable Human Capital Development & Wellbeing
framework.description:
People Pillar:  Inclusive & Equitable Human Capital Development & Well-being
People living in Nigeria have inclusive and equitable human development and well-being

The strategic pillar focuses on ensuring that people living in Nigeria have inclusive and equitable human development and well-being with a focus on the health and education of people in Nigeria and the access to quality basic services.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which ensure that people living in Nigeria have:
1) Equitable access to, and use integrated, comprehensive, high-quality, people centered health services towards attaining Universal Health coverage
2) Equitable access and use of quality education system that delivers an inclusive education for learning and transferable skills
3) Equitable and affordable access to safely managed water and sanitation facilities, and practice safe hygiene and behaviors

children.name: Outcome 3.1: Universal Health Coverage
children.description:
By 2027, people in Nigeria enjoy equitable access to and use of integrated, comprehensive, high-quality, people centered health services towards attaining UHC with a particular focus on AIDS, TB, Malaria and SRHR.

The prioritized transformative initiative to be implemented under this outcome is achieving universal health coverage.

children.name: Output 3.1.1: Health Systems Strengthened Through PHC Inclusive of Health Workforce, Health Financing, Supply Chain and Regulatory Services and Evidence-based Policy Formulation.

Output 3.1.2: Essential Preventive Treatment Care, Health Security and Support Services Systems Strengthened to Address Priority Diseases (HIV/AIDS, TB, Malaria, Hepatitis), Gender-based Violence, Sexual Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal, Child, Adolescent, Older Persons, for People who use Drugs and People in Prison Settings' Health, and Nutrition (RMNCAH+N), Emerging Epidemics/Pandemics and Non-communicable Diseases.
Output 3.1.3: Increase the Demand for and Supply of Gender Sensitive, High Quality, Rights Based SRHR Services for Women, Adolescents, Persons with Disabilities and all Vulnerable Groups.
Outcome 3.2: Quality Education System
children.description:
By 2027, people in Nigeria enjoy equitable access and use of quality education system that delivers an inclusive education for learning and transferable skills.

The prioritized transformative initiative is to "improve learning and scale evidence-based approaches".

children.name: Output 3.2.1: Education Systems Capacity is Strengthened to Plan, Implement and Monitor the Delivery of Basic Quality Inclusive Education for Skills and Knowledge Acquisition Including in Humanitarian Situations.

Output 3.2.2: Government, Communities and Their Partners Demonstrate Increased Capacities to Reduce the Number of Out-of-School Children and Expand Access to Quality Inclusive Education from Pre-primary to Secondary Education Level, Including in Humanitarian and Fragile Contexts.

Output 3.2.3: The Education Eco-system is Better able to Transform the Delivery of Quality Inclusive Basic Education that Rapidly Improves Learning Outcomes from Pre-primary to Secondary Education, Including in Humanitarian and Fragile Contexts.
Outcome 3.3: WASH & Safe Hygiene
children.description: By 2027, people in Nigeria have equitable and affordable access to safely managed water and sanitation facilities, and practice safe hygiene and behaviors.

children.name: Output 3.3.1: Government has Strengthened Capacities to Provide Safe Drinking Water Services in Communities, Schools and Health Facilities Including in Humanitarian Situations.
Output 3.3.2: Government Demonstrates Improved Capacity to Provide Equitable Access to At-least Basic Sanitation Services Including in Humanitarian Situations.
Output 3.3.3: Improved and Sustainable Capacity at National and Sub-national Level for Ending Open Defecation.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 4: Governance, Peace, Security, Access to Justice & Rule of Law
framework.description:
Peace Pillar:  Governance, Peace, Security, Access to Justice & Rule of Law
People living in Nigeria have more inclusive, participatory, transparent and gender equitable governance, gender responsive justice and human rights systems at all levels that promote peaceful, inclusive and a cohesive society.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which ensure that:
1) people living in Nigeria especially the most vulnerable, benefit from peace and security, and protection from conflict violence, and crime through strengthen capacity and infrastructures
2) people living in Nigeria have access to a more accountable, transparent, and gender responsive, and inclusive governance and justice system for the realization of human rights 
3) gender equality and human rights of women, youth, older persons and other marginalized groups including persons with disabilities in Nigeria are enhanced.

children.name: Outcome 4.1: Peace & Security
children.description: By 2027, people in Nigeria of all ages, especially the most vulnerable, benefit from peace and security, and protection from conflict, violence, and crime through strengthen capacity and infrastructures.

children.name: Output 4.1.1: Strengthened Systems, Institutions, and Capacities for Humanitarian Action and Transitioning to Development Solutions, and for Inclusive and Gender Responsive Peace Building.
Output 4.1.2: Strengthened Security Sector Institutions to Reduce Insecurity in Nigeria and Promote Solutions to Cross-border Threats and Challenges.
Output 4.1.3: Strengthened Institutions and Systems to Better Protect People, Environment, and the Economy from Crime, Including Organised Crime.
Outcome 4.2: Inclusive Governance & Justice System
children.description:
By 2027, the people in Nigeria have access to a more accountable, transparent, and gender responsive, and inclusive governance and justice system for the realization of human rights for all especially the most vulnerable population.

The transformative initiative is moving towards strengthened and more accountable governance.

children.name: Output 4.2.1: Rule of Law and Access to Justice, and Respect for Human Rights Advanced Through Improved Capacity of Institutions and Right Holders.
children.description: Tracks the rule of Law, Access to Justice, and Respect for Human Rights through Improved capacity of Institutions and rights holders.

children.name: Output 4.2.2: Capacities Strengthened to Protect Women and Children from Abuse, Exploitation, Trafficking, and all Forms of Violence.
Output 4.2.3: Strengthened systems, Institutions, and Capacities, Including Civil Society for Enhancing Good Governance.
Outcome 4.3: Gender Equality & Human Rights of marginalized groups
children.description:
Gender equality, and human rights of women, youth, older persons and other marginalized groups including persons with disabilities in Nigeria are enhanced.

The transformative initiative is overcoming the national state of emergency created by violence against women and girls.

children.name: Output 4.3.1: Increased Meaningful Participation and Representation of Women, Youth, and Other Marginalised Groups in the Governance Process.

Output 4.3.2: Strengthened Mechanisms and Capacities of Actors and Institutions (Government and Non-government) to Address Discriminatory Gender and Social Norms, and Harmful Practices, Including Child Marriage and Female Genital Mutilation.
Output 4.3.3: Level of Implementation of Accepted Recommendations from the UPR and Human Rights Treaty Bodies.
